newsitem.title: USA: DC plans $25.8 mln tax-lien securitization Nov. 12.
newsitem.headline: DC plans $25.8 mln tax-lien securitization Nov. 12.

text.p: The District of Columbia is planning a $25.8 million securitization of delinquent city tax liens on November 12, Thomas Huestis, the city's deputy CFO for finance said.

The financially strapped District reached agreement with Standard & Poor's Corp for a BBB rating for the offering, Huestis said. Similar deals have been done by only three other U.S. cities -- Jersey City, N.J.; New Haven, Conn.; and New York City, he said.
Huestis said the city is "shooting for" a November 12 sale date for the taxable, private placement offering.
Placement agents are Painewebber Incorporated and Columbia Equity Financial Corp, which is a minority securities firm based in the D.C. area, Huestis said.
"We're expecting a rating of BBB," Huestis said. "We're comfortable with that."
He said a private placement memorandum for the deal will be out next week. The deal is designed to help the city convert a huge backlog of unpaid real estate taxes into millions of dollars in funds.
